X01.title: Crew Vitals simulated crew traces (team-created demo data)

brain.label: Brain and behavior
brain.function: Sleep, mood, stress and alertness support safe work and decision-making.
brain.spaceflight_effects: Isolation, confinement and circadian disruption can affect sleep, mood and performance.

cardiovascular.label: Heart and blood vessels
cardiovascular.function: The heart and blood vessels move blood and regulate pressure.
cardiovascular.spaceflight_effects: Fluid shifts and deconditioning in weightlessness change resting heart rate and pressure regulation, including on return to gravity.

metabolic.label: Metabolism
metabolic.function: Metabolism turns food into usable energy and keeps blood glucose regulated.
metabolic.spaceflight_effects: Stress, low activity and food-system limits can affect metabolism.

musculoskeletal.label: Bones and muscles
musculoskeletal.function: Bones and muscles support movement and strength.
musculoskeletal.spaceflight_effects: Without gravity loading, bone and muscle are lost. Daily aerobic and resistive exercise is the main countermeasure.

immune.label: Immune system (whole body)
immune.function: The immune system defends against infection.
immune.spaceflight_effects: Immune function can shift in spaceflight. Fever is an early sign of infection.

radiation.label: Radiation exposure (whole body)
radiation.function: A personal dosimeter badge tracks how much radiation a crew member receives over time.
radiation.spaceflight_effects: Outside Earth's protective magnetic field and atmosphere, radiation exposure accumulates over a mission.

sleep_duration.label: Sleep duration
sleep_duration.how_measured: Wrist actigraphy or wearable, plus a morning sleep log.
sleep_duration.why: Circadian disruption and fatigue raise error risk.
contact_when: Under 6 hours for several days together with mood or performance decline
limitations: Wearable sleep estimates differ from lab sleep studies.

mood.label: Mood (self-rated 1–5)
mood.how_measured: Short opt-in self-rating on a 1 to 5 scale.
mood.why: Can be an early sign of behavioral health decline.
limitations: Self-ratings are subjective. A coarse 1–5 scale often has too little spread for a statistical baseline (shown as 'insufficient scale').

stress.label: Stress (self-rated 1–5)
stress.how_measured: Short opt-in self-rating on a 1 to 5 scale.
stress.why: Can be an early sign of behavioral health decline.
contact_when: Persistently high stress with low mood
limitations: Self-ratings are subjective. A coarse 1–5 scale often has too little spread for a statistical baseline (shown as 'insufficient scale').

resting_heart_rate.label: Resting heart rate
resting_heart_rate.how_measured: Wrist wearable or chest strap; manual pulse count as backup.
resting_heart_rate.why: Fluid shifts and deconditioning change resting rate.
limitations: Wearable readings are affected by motion and fit.

systolic_bp.label: Blood pressure (systolic)
systolic_bp.how_measured: Automated upper-arm cuff, seated, two readings.
systolic_bp.why: Pressure regulation changes in weightlessness and on return to gravity.
contact_when: Repeated readings far outside personal range
limitations: Single readings vary; the guide recommends two seated readings.

diastolic_bp.label: Blood pressure (diastolic)
diastolic_bp.how_measured: Automated upper-arm cuff, seated, two readings.
diastolic_bp.why: Pressure regulation changes in weightlessness and on return to gravity.
contact_when: Repeated readings far outside personal range
limitations: Single readings vary; the guide recommends two seated readings.

blood_glucose.label: Blood glucose (fasting)
blood_glucose.why: Stress, low activity and food-system limits affect metabolism.
self_care: If high: hydrate, do light exercise and review meals
contact_when: Repeated readings below 60 or above 125 mg/dL (demo rule, to be confirmed)
limitations: Fingerstick meters have measurement error, and readings depend on fasting state.

body_temperature.label: Body temperature
body_temperature.why: Fever is an early infection sign when immune function shifts.
contact_when: Fever lasting more than a day
Temperature above 38 °C (demo rule, to be confirmed)
limitations: Forehead thermometers are less precise than oral ones.

radiation_badge_daily_dose.label: Personal dosimeter badge (daily)
contact_when: Cumulative dose near the career limit
limitations: A badge reading is not effective dose or cancer risk. The NASA instrument panel is separate historical context and is not this person's dose.

exercise_minutes.label: Exercise (aerobic + resistive)
exercise_minutes.why: Main countermeasure for bone and muscle loss.
self_care: Schedule the full daily aerobic and resistive protocol
limitations: Logged minutes do not measure exercise intensity or bone and muscle status.

station.label: ISS / Station
station.one_way_delay: Near real time (seconds), with occasional loss-of-signal periods
station.reply_expectation: A flight surgeon can usually respond during the same session.
station.guidance: Contact the flight surgeon directly and follow their instructions.

spacecraft.label: Spacecraft
spacecraft.reply_expectation: Near-live conversation is possible, but links may be scheduled.
spacecraft.guidance: Start the interim steps, then contact the flight surgeon at the next link.

lunar.label: Lunar base
lunar.reply_expectation: Conversation works with a short lag.
lunar.guidance: Start the interim steps and contact the flight surgeon.

mars.label: Mars transit
mars.one_way_delay: Grows with distance, to about 20 minutes one way near Mars
mars.reply_expectation: A reply can take 40 minutes or more round trip. Do not wait idle.
mars.guidance: Follow the interim steps now. Send the flight surgeon a written summary with your readings, then recheck while you wait.

environment_note: Delay figures are approximate light-time and need confirming against NASA sources (Member 1).
